one_line: Major AI firms secured billions in funding and IPO plans amid a broader tech sell-off and infrastructure pushback, while advancing mathematical reasoning proofs.

themes.title: Funding and market pressures mount
themes.text: OpenAI closed $11 billion in funding at a $1.25 trillion valuation, while Anthropic pressed forward with November IPO plans despite a $5.7 trillion Wall Street market rout and warnings that the AI investment cycle may have peaked.

stories.headline: Anthropic presses on with November IPO plans despite global AI stock sell-off
OpenAI closes $11 billion in funding at $1.25 trillion valuation
Wall Street grapples with $5.7 trillion rout as AI bets unwind
AI investment cycle may have peaked, Jefferies warns

themes.title: Models solve long-standing mathematical problems
themes.text: AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic disproved the 27-year-old Exponential Time Hypothesis and proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, with both proofs formally verified using the Lean proof assistant.

stories.headline: Physical Superintelligence AI system proves Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
OpenAI and Anthropic AI models disprove Exponential Time Hypothesis

themes.title: Infrastructure expansion faces local pushback
themes.text: Following local voter rejections of data centers in midterm elections, OpenAI changed its data center policies to end public official non-disclosure agreements and cover full electricity costs, while Google acquired Crusoe's pre-developed Wyoming data center site.

stories.headline: Google acquires southeast Wyoming data center site from Crusoe
OpenAI changes data center policies after midterm voter pushback
